Ninety-one percent of materials handling professionals surveyed by Modern Materials Handling said they like their current job , up from 88% a year earlier. In the same survey, 88% described their job as at least somewhat stressful.
What’s Related
The 2026 survey also found that 97% would recommend materials handling as a career, the highest share in four years. Fifty-two percent said they were very satisfied with their career, and another 22% were extremely satisfied.
Peerless Research Group surveyed 117 qualified Modern Materials Handling subscribers for the 19th annual study. Manufacturing accounted for the largest share of respondents. The survey also included people working in wholesale and retail trade , transportation and warehousing .
“People who are in materials handling and supply chain really love the profession, and there’s lots of room for growth and opportunity,” said Michelle Rohlwing, innovation, product development and learning manager at the Institute for Supply Management .
RELATED: 2026 Salary Survey: Average Materials Handling Pay Dips Under $100K | What Logistics and Supply Chain Jobs Pay in 2026
Too much work
Among respondents who called their jobs very or extremely stressful, 42% pointed to workload, the most common answer for the third year in a row. Too few people to get the job done and outdated technology tied for second, each cited by 35%.
Across all respondents, 53% called their jobs somewhat stressful, 26% described them as very stressful, and 9% called them extremely stressful. The remaining 12% said their jobs were either not very stressful or not stressful at all.
Among those who described their jobs as very or extremely stressful, concern about company stability rose more than any other factor. Twenty-two percent cited it, up from 7% in 2025. The share who pointed to a lack of career development fell from 25% to 16%, and 3% cited a poor relationship with their boss, down from 8%.
Longtime workers show loyalty
Respondents averaged 18.5 years in materials handling. Nearly a third had spent 20 to 29 years in the field, and another 19% had spent 30 years or more. Seventeen percent had less than five years of experience.
They stayed with their employers, too, averaging 10.4 years with their current company. Twenty-eight percent had been there for at least 20 years. Respondents had worked for an average of 2.7 companies over their materials handling careers, and 16% had worked for only one.
Three more findings from the survey
Job satisfaction and career satisfaction moved in different directions. The share who liked their current job rose from 88% to 91%, while the share who were very or extremely satisfied with their career fell from 78% to 74%.
Work pressure carried over into home life. Among respondents who described their jobs as very or extremely stressful, 34% cited balancing work and home life, and 29% said they didn’t have enough time to get their work done.
Management decisions added to the pressure. In that same group, 31% cited questionable management decisions, up from 28% in 2025.
